Changes for Nova Scotia (BPANS); step 5, Nova Scotia (LCP); tables 8.1 and 8.2

Nova Scotia rates 8.79%, 14.95%, 16.67%, 17.5% and 21% from 30,995, 61,991, 97,417 and 157,124; basic personal amount 11,932, the same for every income since the BPANS formula is removed for 2026; labour-sponsored funds credit LCP of 20% of the shares withheld, at most 2,000 a year.
TD1NS 2026 Nova Scotia Personal Tax Credits Return
Line 1 (basic personal amount) and the total claim amount
Nova Scotia basic personal amount of 11,932 for 2026 and the total claim amount TCP entered on the contract.
Personal income tax rates and indexation
Nova Scotia taxable income brackets of 2026 (8.79% to 30,995, 14.95% to 61,991, 16.67% to 97,417, 17.5% to 157,124, 21% above) and basic personal amount of 11,932; indexation rate of 1.6% for 2026.
Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia
Maximum of the next year and table of the previous years

Maximum assessable earnings per worker, effective January 1: 76,300 in 2025, 79,900 in 2026, 83,300 in 2027; 135.7% of the Nova Scotia average industrial wage. Employers pay premiums only on the earnings of a worker up to the maximum.
Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia
Premium = rate per $100 x assessable payroll, the gross earnings of the covered workers each up to the yearly maximum. Each employer is notified on September 1 of its rate for the next calendar year.
Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia

Rate of an employer = rate of its industry rate group adjusted by experience rating, plus the safety association levy and a surcharge where they apply. Average rate 2.65 per $100 of assessable payroll, 2.25 from January 1, 2027.
Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia
Monthly or quarterly report of the assessable payroll, by pay date, with the payment, due the 15th of the month that follows the reporting period, even for a nil payroll.
Workers' Compensation Board of Nova Scotia

Coverage mandatory in a mandatory industry with 3 or more workers at the same time; officers and directors active in the business count as workers; proprietors and partners are not workers and may buy optional coverage.
Sections 41 (maximum gross annual earnings) and 124 (assessable payroll)

Maximum gross annual earnings: a percentage of the average industrial wage for the Province set by the Governor in Council (s. 41(c)); the payroll on which the Board assesses an employer excludes the remuneration of a worker above that maximum (s. 124(2)).
Sections 1A (assessable payroll), 22 (maximum earnings) and 35 (reporting and remittance)

Assessable payroll: the employment earnings of box 14 of the T4 slips. Maximum earnings: 135.7% of the average industrial wage for Nova Scotia of the 12 months ending March 31 of the previous year, rounded to the nearest 100. Assessable payroll reported and assessments remitted at the same time as the remittances to the CRA, unless the Board approves otherwise.
